name: The Angel Arms Foundation
tagline: Horse-assisted therapy, learning and care for children with special needs, and a new purpose for retired horses.

contact.address: Farm de Lek, Khlong 15, Rangsit–Nakhon Nayok Road, Ongkharak District, Nakhon Nayok, Thailand

mission: To offer horse-assisted and movement-based therapy, learning opportunities, safer homes, and volunteer-led community programs for children and young people with special needs from families facing hardship, while giving retired and injured horses a new purpose as therapy partners.
vision: To provide comprehensive, inclusive, and sustainable assistance and support to improve quality of life and well-being, while promoting holistic development and education for children, young people, and persons with special needs.

values.title: Dream
values.text: Fun, play and the joy of giving. Every child deserves to dream, including the dream to ride.

values.title: Hope
values.text: Our Guardian Angels, the horses, bring hope to children and are given a second chance themselves.

values.title: Friends
values.text: A community where parents, volunteers and friends can say “I can help” and “I need help”.

values.title: Love
values.text: Love without expectation: care, patience and time for families to talk, reflect and grow together.

background: Farm de Lek has operated for more than 10 years to promote learning and development for children and young people. It is located at Khlong 15, Rangsit–Nakhon Nayok Road, Ongkharak District, Nakhon Nayok Province.

Mrs Premruedee Tantivejkul, an executive of Farm de Lek, found that many children and young people still do not have the opportunity to achieve a good quality of life or access high-quality support to develop their potential. This is especially true for learning spaces outside the classroom, due to limited financial resources and a lack of government support, particularly for children with special needs.

For 10 years Farm de Lek has supported learning activities and child-development programs for children with disabilities and special needs from the Maha Chakri Sirindhorn Special Education Centre, Nakhon Nayok, under the Ministry of Education. This has included early assistance, preparing children to enter early childhood centres, kindergartens, inclusive and specialised schools, training for caregivers, and rehabilitation services within families and communities.

After many years of this work, the team found that children with special needs, both those supported by special education centres and many who cannot reach their services, still need help to live with a good quality of life. So the Farm de Lek Learning Centre, led by Mrs Premruedee Tantivejkul, is establishing The Angel Arms Foundation.
method: Our therapy follows the principles of the Horseboy Method and Movement Method developed by Mr Rupert Isaacson.
objectives: Rehabilitate and enhance the development of children and young people with special needs through horses and movement, following the principles of the Horseboy Method and Movement Method by Mr Rupert Isaacson.
Create learning opportunities and enrich life experiences for children and young people with special needs whose families face hardship.
Promote and support access to education and sustainable developmental support for children and young people with special needs whose families face hardship.
Promote and support the development of educational resources and human resources to improve the quality of life of children and young people with special needs.
Support improvements to the environment and housing of children, young people, and persons with special needs and their families, so that living conditions are appropriate, safe, clean and hygienic.
Provide knowledge and encourage community participation through volunteer programs and activities for public benefit.
Promote learning and provide experience for school students, university students, young people, and members of the public who are interested in studying and working in multidisciplinary fields.
Take in, care for, and develop retired horses, and rehabilitate horses injured through work, so that they can be used in therapy for children and persons with special needs.
